Definition: 60-dB high-frequency hearing limit
Note: Printed hearing-range endpoint at 60 dB SPL, not the maximum tested frequency (11.2 kHz). Same primary observation as TABLEI 5.9 kHz; deduplicate. Gate: DEDUP_TABLEI_SAME_PRIMARY_OBSERVATION. Definitions are method-specific; no central standardized-term changes.
Source Note: PDF p. 5 / printed p. 210, Results > Audiogram, continuation from p. 209; abstract PDF p. 1 / printed p. 206 corroborates

Definition: Best-hearing frequency
Note: Distinct point of most sensitive hearing at 1 kHz; species-summary result for two animals. Same observation as TABLEI best frequency 1 kHz. Gate: DEDUP_TABLEI_SAME_PRIMARY_OBSERVATION. Definitions are method-specific; no central standardized-term changes.
Source Note: PDF p. 4 / printed p. 209, Results > Audiogram, final paragraph; abstract PDF p. 1 / printed p. 206 corroborates

Definition: Lowest auditory threshold
Note: Lowest threshold 32 dB SPL at the best-hearing frequency of 1 kHz; source audiometric criterion is corrected detection performance 0.50. Same observation as TABLEI lowest threshold 32 dB. Gate: DEDUP_TABLEI_SAME_PRIMARY_OBSERVATION. Definitions are method-specific; no central standardized-term changes.
Source Note: PDF p. 4 / printed p. 209, Results > Audiogram, final paragraph; abstract PDF p. 1 / printed p. 206 corroborates

Definition: Failure to localize a single 100-ms noise burst at 180 degrees
Note: Both animals unable to localize a single 100-ms noise burst at 180-degree separation despite weeks of training. This is a categorical failure, not a measured 180-degree threshold and not zero acuity. Gate: CATEGORICAL_FAILURE_NOT_NUMERIC_ACUITY. Definitions are method-specific; no central standardized-term changes.
Source Note: PDF p. 5 / printed p. 210, Results > Sound localization > Effect of signal duration, first paragraph; Fig. 3 caption corroborates

Definition: Localization threshold for a train of three 700-ms noise bursts
Note: Printed thresholds of 29 degrees for a train of three 700-ms bursts separated by 100 ms. Not comparable to brief-sound thresholds of surface rodents; no figure digitization and no inferred individual A/B thresholds. Gate: LONG_TRAIN_ONLY_NOT_BRIEF_SOUND_MAA. Definitions are method-specific; no central standardized-term changes.
Source Note: PDF p. 5 / printed p. 210, Results > Sound localization > Acuity, second paragraph, right column

Definition: Average localization threshold for a single 400-ms noise burst
Note: Printed average threshold was 180 degrees for a single 400-ms burst; neither animal discriminated 90-degree separation above chance. Value read from prose, not digitized from Fig. 4. Different stimulus condition from 29-degree result. Gate: SINGLE_400MS_ONLY_NOT_100MS_MAA. Definitions are method-specific; no central standardized-term changes.
Source Note: PDF p. 5 / printed p. 210, Results > Sound localization > Acuity, second paragraph, right column
